items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Sentiment Analysis in Pregnancy-Related Weight Discussions on Reddit: Human Performance-Aligned Comparative Evaluation Study
items.abstract: Background Pregnancy-related weight gain is both physiologically complex and socially charged, and online discussions often combine clinical information with implicit emotional distress. Although automated sentiment analysis could support research on pregnancy-related discourse, model performance in this context remains inadequately characterized relative to expert human judgment. Objective This study aimed to benchmark contemporary sentiment classification models on pregnancy-related weight discussions, with emphasis on agreement with expert consensus, interpretive ambiguity, task adaptation, and deployment across posts and comments. Methods We curated 15,619 Reddit posts and comments using a large language model (LLM)–guided keyword expansion strategy and established an adjudicated consensus reference set of 200 posts. We evaluated 10 models on a fixed held-out test set (N=150) using aligned text inputs, weighted performance metrics, and 1000-resample bootstrap CIs. RoBERTa (Robustly Optimized Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers Approach) and BERTweet (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers for Tweets) were additionally evaluated in a 5-fold fine-tuning sensitivity analysis. Gemini-3-Flash (Google DeepMind [Google LLC]) and Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT)–OSS (OpenAI) were then applied to 400 unlabeled posts and 15,019 comments with intermodel agreement assessment. To expand expert-labeled coverage, a separate 106-post annotation extension was used for secondary evaluation of the 2 models carried forward to post-level corpus inference, and cross-source recoverability of the API-derived retrieval was assessed using Arctic Shift (Arthur Heitmann). Results The 2 primary experts (FAK and BMW) achieved 59.0% preadjudication agreement (Cohen κ=0.344). In the fixed held-out comparison, Gemini-3-Flash had the numerically highest weighted F 1 -score of 0.662 (κ=0.478), followed by GPT-OSS ( F 1 -score=0.645; κ=0.436), with overlapping CIs across leading models. Under the harmonized direct-argmax decision rule with minimally processed text, BERTweet achieved an F 1 -score of 0.623 (κ=0.369), and RoBERTa achieved an F 1 -score of 0.605 (κ=0.339). In the separate fine-tuning sensitivity analysis, the mean cross-validated F 1 -score was 0.708 (SD 0.087) for RoBERTa and 0.616 (SD 0.079) for BERTweet. Among Gemini-3-Flash errors, 55.8% (29/52) occurred in posts on which the 2 primary experts disagreed. In the 106-post annotation extension, primary-expert agreement was 64.2% (68/106; κ=0.367); Gemini-3-Flash and GPT-OSS achieved weighted F 1 -score values of 0.633 and 0.680, respectively, and both identified 56 of 58 expert-negative posts in an exploratory human-review prioritization analysis. All 714 API-retrieved post IDs were independently recoverable through Arctic Shift. Intermodel agreement was 92.3% for posts (κ=0.797; n=400 valid pairs) and 46.3% for comments (κ=0.102; n=1500). Conclusions No single model architecture was uniformly superior, and performance depended on the adaptation regime, annotation ambiguity, and discourse type. These findings define important boundary conditions for sentiment analysis of naturalistic maternal-health discourse: broad polarity classification can support corpus prioritization and hypothesis generation but is insufficient as a stand-alone measure of patient experience.

items.title: Between Happiness and Success: The Contribution of Subjective Well-Being and Motivation to Academic Achievement in HSE University Students
items.abstract: In recent years, among students of leading universities, there has been an alarming dynamics of deterioration of their psychological state, which is expressed, among other things, in the suicidal behavior of students. Indicators of subjective well-being and internal motivation of students are not only at a low level, but also continue to decline with each year of study, while according to the self-determination theory, high efficiency (providing the ability to study in a highly selective university) should be supported by exactly these factors. In connection with this contradiction, the question arises: is the influence of subjective well-being and motivation on a person's success as unambiguous as it is commonly believed, or are there different profiles of motivational and emotional regulation that allow you to gain high achievements? This article is devoted to the study of the impact of the relationship between subjective well-being and various types of academic motivation on the level of academic achievements. The results of cluster and comparative analysis of the obtained data are presented. The sample of the study consisted of 209 students of bachelor's and master's degrees of various specialties of HSE. Statistical analysis showed that combinations of negative affect with extrinsic motivation and positive affect with intrinsic motivation contribute to the formation of two alternative profiles that do not affect academic success and involvement, but are reflected in the level of student well-being. It is noteworthy that the distinctive characteristics of students with high academic performance are high motivation for achievement and low negative affect. The problematic issues of well-being and motivation in the academic environment are discussed, the question of the problematic nature of external motivation in the university for the well-being of students is raised.

items.title: Between hype and uncertainty: Expert assessments of nuclear small-modular reactors (SMRs) under data center energy boom
items.abstract: The unprecedented growth in artificial intelligence and data center energy demand has renewed interest in small modular reactors (SMRs) as a potential low-carbon baseload solution. Yet significant uncertainty persists around the techno-economic characteristics and policy solutions necessary for SMR commercialization in the United States. This inadvertently leaves policymakers navigating critical decisions about resource allocation, regulatory reform, and long-term energy planning without a clear picture of near-term prospects of SMRs. This study addresses that gap by conducting a mixed methods expert survey of 33 professionals from industry, academia, government, utilities, and think tanks. Results collectively suggest a moderate confidence in an outlook with high overnight capital cost of over $6000/kW and cost overruns of over 30%, falling short of DOE's commercialization target. They also reflect cautious optimism rooted in the expectation of an incremental learning rate due to rapid electricity demand growth from data centers and standardization of design. Overall, experts highlight a significant gap between promotional narratives and realistic techno-economic trajectories.

items.title: Between the Lines: Multi-turn Contextual Investment Advice Detection
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly power financial conversational assistants, detecting investment advice in natural language has become a critical regulatory and safety challenge. Unlike explicit single-turn recommendations, investment advice often emerges implicitly and progressively over multi-turn conversations, shaped by user intent, delivery style, and contextual buildup. We introduce the first comprehensive framework for detecting both sequential and contextual investment advice in dialogue settings. Central to our approach is a modular, top-down synthetic data generation pipeline that systematically spans a taxonomy of advisory trajectories using an axis-bucket-descriptor schema. We simulate both benign and high-risk conversations across diverse user personas, financial instruments, and risk tiers, and evaluate detection capabilities using LLM-as-a-Judge with entropy-based uncertainty diagnostics. Our results show that contextual advisory detection remains substantially more challenging than sequential cases, even under few-shot prompting with tailored demonstrations. This work lays the foundation for scalable guardrail development in high-stakes, compliance-sensitive domains, where advisory risk is often subtle, distributed, and perception-dependent.

items.title: Beyond accuracy: The PRIME framework for ethical human-AI collaboration in radiology
items.abstract: Purpose Generative AI changes the radiologist's task from judging AI output to editing and signing text that AI drafted. Existing guidance covers automation bias, local validation and monitoring, but gives little direction on verifying generated text, recording its provenance, or auditing reliance on it. Approach This paper consolidates multisociety statements, consensus guidelines, human-factors evidence and the EU legal framework as of October 2026 into a practice framework, and applies it to assistive, case-allocation, autonomous and generative workflows. Framework PRIME has five principles at two levels. Primacy of accountability, rigorous verification and maintained expertise apply to the radiologist; informed transparency and earned trust through oversight apply to the institution. A recorded independent read before AI output is viewed links four principles: it serves as the omission search, keeps unassisted skill in routine work, supplies the data for reliance metrics, and documents the radiologist's own judgment. Verification is split into checking AI statements and searching for omissions. Provenance is recorded per statement and paired with local performance data. Monitoring uses an independent reference sample, because audits against the signed report miss errors that radiologists accepted. Implications Each principle names an actor, an action, an indicator and a trigger, and is mapped to the AI Act, the Medical Device Regulation, the General Data Protection Regulation and product liability law. Most rules are design proposals that still require clinical evaluation, and the framework does not resolve liability or structural inequity.

items.title: Can Voluntary Corporate Transparency Curb Corruption? Community-Level Evidence from Oil and Gas Fields in Africa
items.abstract: Voluntary corporate transparency seeks to promote accountability through disclosure, but substantive reporting does not by itself guarantee societal benefits. We examine whether this form of self-regulation can help curb corruption where formal oversight is weak, focusing on corporate support for the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI), a multistakeholder initiative that promotes disclosure of company payments to host governments. We link geolocated data on African oil and gas fields and their operators to Afrobarometer surveys and satellite nighttime-light measures and estimate difference-in-differences models that track changes in outcomes around the same fields before and after operators endorse the EITI. We find that corporate EITI support is associated with lower perceived corruption and less reported bribery, greater civic engagement, greater perceived freedom to speak, and higher nighttime-light intensity, a proxy for local economic activity. The association with lower perceived corruption is stronger around fields with nearby NGO or aid-project activity, among residents living closer to fields, and among frequent users of traditional news media. Supplementary analyses provide indirect evidence that supporting firms were more transparent before mandatory disclosure laws took effect, and show that they had fewer joint-venture partners and larger ownership stakes after endorsement. Archival cases from Nigeria and Ghana illustrate how civil-society organizations and journalists use extractive-industry information to question firms and public authorities. The findings point to local governance benefits of voluntary transparency commitments and are consistent with an information-to-accountability account in which these benefits depend on both substantive reporting and local opportunities to scrutinize and use the information.

items.title: CHOOSING AND CONSIDERING BODY SHAPES IN MODERN CLOTHING DESIGN: ARTISTIC-CONSTRUCTIVE AND SOCIO-PSYCHOLOGICAL ASPECTS
items.abstract: This article analyzes the peculiarities of choosing and considering body shapes when creating modern clothing designs, exploring its artistic-constructive and socio-psychological aspects. In the contemporary fashion industry, couturiers and designers no longer limit themselves to standard templates; instead, they focus heavily on the plasticity, proportions, and visual correction of diverse body structures. The article provides a theoretical and scientific justification for the role of lines, fabric textures, color harmony, and constructive solutions in garment design for various body types. Furthermore, it highlights the principles of creating ergonomically and aesthetically flawless garments by ensuring a harmonious balance between the consumer's individual identity and physical form. The study also considers the methodological stages of the design process, the influence of age and cultural context, the relationship between sizing systems and body morphology, and the growing importance of inclusivity and sustainability in contemporary fashion.

items.title: Cleopatra’s Motivation and Power in H. Rider Haggard’s Cleopatra
items.abstract: This article examines the motivations that drive Cleopatra to fight against her brother, Ptolemy, in H. Rider Haggard’s Cleopatra (1889). The study develops a qualitative literary analysis of the novel through close attention to dialogue, character action, political decisions, and recurring patterns of conflict. The analysis distinguishes between intrinsic motivation and power motivation and then examines how these dimensions intersect rather than operate independently. The findings identify two major intrinsic motives—desire for Egyptian independence and concern for legacy and dynastic continuity—and five major power motives: political ambition, personal rivalry, strategic calculation, manipulation and control, and personal survival. Empirical textual evidence shows that these motives are repeatedly converted into concrete political practices, including mobilizing Egyptians, preparing military forces, seeking alliances, approaching Julius Caesar, challenging Ptolemy’s legitimacy, manipulating factions, and protecting Cleopatra’s political position. The discussion demonstrates that national sovereignty and personal ambition are not mutually exclusive within the novel: Cleopatra presents the consolidation of her authority as a means of securing Egypt’s future, while her pursuit of sovereignty simultaneously strengthens her personal power. Maslow’s hierarchy of needs is employed cautiously as an interpretive framework. Recent empirical research challenges the assumption that human needs are universally satisfied in a fixed sequence, supporting a more integrated interpretation of Cleopatra’s simultaneous pursuit of security, belonging, esteem, agency, and self-realization.

items.title: Conceptual foundations of design and technological interfaces
items.abstract: This chapter examines the technological interface from a sociotechnical and interdisciplinary perspective.It describes the shift from the functionalist paradigm, which valued products by algorithmic performance, electronic stability and compliance with technical requirements, towards user-centred design, which holds that interactive systems must adapt to people's needs, cognitive limitations and contexts of use.Within this framework, usability and aesthetics are presented not as ornamental or independent attributes but as dimensions to be integrated.The chapter treats hardware and software as a single sociotechnical system: hardware provides the material canvas in which aesthetics first appears, while software shapes the interactive dynamics in which usability is experienced.The graphical user interface (GUI) is therefore addressed as the core of interaction, the space where functional and visual attributes converge.The approach is a conceptual, descriptive-analytical review of human-computer interaction literature, covering event-driven programming and GUI components such as icons, windows, pointing devices, menus and buttons, together with a brief historical account from Xerox PARC to the Macintosh and touchscreen devices.Drawing on this literature, the chapter states that interfaces based on visual metaphors and icons reduce the learning curve and cognitive load, and that an imbalance between hardware and software quickly undermines both aesthetics and actual usability.It concludes that a holistic, interactive approach grounded in user needs is required for products to be competitive, with user-centred design proposed as the framework for integrating usability and aesthetics in organizational settings.

items.title: Confidently Wrong: Detecting Hallucinations in Financial Question Answering from LLM Internal States
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in financial applications fail most consequentially when they are confidently wrong. Hedged, uncertain answers invite scrutiny, whereas confident errors silently degrade downstream decisions without warning. We ask how reliably such confidently wrong answers, or confident hallucinations, can be detected from a model’s internal activations, and whether those activations carry information beyond its output-level confidence signals. We train linear probes on the residual stream and evaluate them on two established numerical question-answering (QA) benchmarks built from real filings, FinQA and TAT-QA. Behavioral confidence is measured as the agreement among eight resampled answers to the same question, and probe effectiveness is compared against baselines, such as token log-probabilities and the model’s own True/False self-assessment of its answer. Our findings show that among confident answers, those for which all eight resamples agree, 15–23% are wrong on FinQA. There the probes have a significant advantage over output-level baselines in detecting hallucinations, holding 0.68–0.77 AUROC while the best baselines fall to 0.55–0.63, across Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Gemma-2-9B. Our results suggest that probing can be a cost-effective triage mechanism for routing LLM answers to human review and quality control procedures in high-stakes financial applications. Code and data are available at https://github.com/richardzhewang/confidently-wrong.

items.title: Conversational Capture: A Trajectory-Level Framework for Evaluating Generative Engine Optimization in Multi-turn Human-Agent Interaction
items.abstract: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) shapes content to increase its likelihood of being cited by answer engines built on retrieval-augmented large language models. GEO is typically evaluated as a single-turn property: for a fixed query, an evaluator measures a source’s visibility in one answer. We argue that the single answer is an inadequate unit of analysis. Human-agent information seeking forms a closed loop. The agent’s answer changes the user’s beliefs and therefore the next question, which in turn determines what the agent retrieves. We introduce conversational capture, a phenomenon in which a source cited early becomes substantially more likely to be cited again. Capture operates through a machine-side channel, history-conditioned retrieval, and a human-side channel, follow-up questions directed toward the captured source. This persistence can be independent of the source’s current relevance. We formalize the interaction as a two-layer closed-loop system and derive computable trajectory-level constructs: cumulative conversational visibility; a decomposition of trajectory gain into a single-turn "direct" term and a closed-loop "feedback" term; a nested counterfactual split of the feedback term into machine-side and human-side channels; a capture coefficient; a compounding ratio; and a misranking diagnostic. Using reinforcement-process (Pólya-urn) theory, we prove that the feedback term is identically zero under single-turn evaluation and that GEO’s cumulative payoff grows superlinearly with conversation length while capture develops. A model-derived illustration shows that the feedback term can exceed the direct term, the compounding ratio exceeds two within ten turns, and the single-turn and trajectory rankings of GEO methods agree only weakly (Kendall’s τ = 0.4). Thus, single-turn evaluation can select the wrong method. We connect the human channel to information foraging, trust calibration, and Bayesian persuasion, and discuss design implications for answer engines.

items.title: Decoding decision correctness from EEG under high cognitive workload in virtual reality: implications for collaborative brain-computer interface teams
items.abstract: Introduction Collaborative Brain-Computer Interfaces (cBCIs) offer a promising mechanism to augment team decision‐making, but existing approaches rely exclusively on evidence available only after a decision has been made and reported, such as reaction time or stated confidence. This limits their use to explaining or discounting a decision after the fact, rather than informing a teams response before it is finalised. We tested whether spatial‐covariance EEG features could instead provide a genuinely pre-emptive signal of an operators decision correctness, available within the response window itself, and whether such a signal depends on cognitive workload. Methods Using a continuous virtual reality target-detection task, participants (N = 23) completed a within-subject visual workload manipulation (High vs. Low), implemented via a Degraded Visual Environment. Results A Riemannian tangent‐space classifier, trained on a strictly motor‐safe EEG window preceding each response, decoded Correct from Incorrect decisions with above‐chance accuracy under High Workload (61.4%, p = .0014, N = 23) but not reliably under Low Workload (N = 17), where near‐ceiling behavioural accuracy left too few error trials for valid classification. Ablation analysis showed the signal was carried predominantly by posterior occipito‐parietal channels, consistent with a perceptual rather than motor origin. At the team level, weighting votes by this pre-emptive neural signal, available before a response is committed, produced substantial accuracy gains on contested (evenly‐split) trials under High Workload (57% to 88% as team size increased from 2 to 16), but was actively detrimental under Low Workload. Discussion Critically, this advantage held even against post‐hoc behavioural signals: confidence was the strongest single team‐level signal overall, but by definition cannot inform a decision still in progress, whereas the neural signal can. These findings indicate that EEG‐based decision‐reliability signals are not a general‐purpose team augmentation tool, but a workload‐conditional one, with clear implications for when and how cBCI systems should be deployed in operational teams.

items.title: Delegating or Doing? Understanding User Behavior in Hybrid Human–Agent Interfaces
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded into applications, allowing users to complete tasks either through direct manipulation or by delegating actions to conversational agents. However, little is known about how users balance these modalities when both are available. We present a web-based content management system augmented with an LLM agent through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling users to perform CRUD tasks through a graphical interface, a conversational agent, or both. We conducted a between-subjects study (N=73) comparing three interaction modes: Traditional-Only, AI-First, and Hybrid. Across sixteen scenarios, we analyzed task completion time, interaction logs, and delegation behavior. AI-assisted interaction significantly reduced clicks, page navigations, and scrolling, indicating lower interaction effort. Surprisingly, these reductions did not translate into faster task completion, as task duration did not differ significantly across conditions. We also found no significant relationship between CRUD operation type and delegation, suggesting that users did not systematically avoid delegating higher-risk actions. Instead, delegation varied far more between participants than between tasks, with individual differences accounting for roughly half the variance in assistant use (ICC =.50). Our findings suggest that the primary benefit of human–agent interfaces may be reducing interaction effort rather than improving speed, and that delegation reflects who the user is more than what the task demands.

items.title: Design and Ergonomic Evaluation of an Automated Wheelchair Lifting Aid for Caregiver Injury Prevention
items.abstract: Background: Manual handling during wheelchair loading and unloading imposes substantial biomechanical demands on caregivers, potentially contributing to work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) because of non-neutral working postures and increased spinal loading, particularly at the L5/S1 lumbosacral junction. Objective: This study proposes the design, development, and ergonomic evaluation of an electromechanical assistive lifting device integrated into the cargo compartment of a Toyota Avanza multipurpose vehicle (MPV). Methods: A 12-V DC electric winch equipped with a swiveling boom arm and a quick-release sling harness was evaluated during caregiver-assisted wheelchair loading and unloading tasks involving three wheelchair configurations: a standard manual wheelchair (17 kg), a Type A powered wheelchair, and a Type B powered wheelchair (weighing up to 28 kg). Functional compatibility and observable caregiver working postures were assessed before and after device implementation. Results: Automated lifting system successfully demonstrated proof-of-concept operation with all three wheelchair configurations. Conclusion: Proof-of-concept device demonstrated functional feasibility and the potential to reduce non-neutral caregiver postures during wheelchair loading and unloading. items.title: Design and Implementation of a Grid-Independent, Non-Destructive Assistive Telemetry Node for Transitory and Rental Space Accessibility
items.abstract: Conventional domestic entry notification frameworks rely predominantly on acoustic propagation, presenting an institutionalized accessibility barrier for the deaf and hard-of-hearing demographic. While localized visual or haptic retrofitting solutions exist for permanent installations, they remain highly impractical for transitory, short-term rental, or travel accommodations where structural and electrical grid modifications are legally or structurally prohibited. This paper presents a novel, grid-independent, non-destructive assistive telemetry node designed specifically for temporary or mobile spatial environments. Utilizing a RISC-V based ESP32-C3 microcontroller, the system circumvents local spatial constraints by routing hardware-interrupt-driven trigger events over an automated network captive portal directly to a secure cloud broker (Telegram Bot API). The alert payload is translated at the user's mobile endpoint into multi-modal haptic-visual feedback streams, ensuring unconstrained geographical tracking. The hardware layer is packaged inside a custom additive-manufactured Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol (PETG) enclosure optimized for rugged field mobility and tool-free deployment. Electrical characterization yields an optimized deep-sleep quiescent current floor of 7.2µA sustained via an ultra-low-power low-dropout (LDO) linear regulator stage. Empirical evaluations across eighteen distinct evaluation iterations demonstrate an overall mean end-to-end network latency of 5.86 seconds and a 100% transmission success rate, translating to a mathematically validated operational battery deployment shelf-life exceeding 14 to 16 months on standard commercial alkaline cells. Qualitative field evaluations with an assistive user cohort verify that the multi-modal notification pipeline significantly enhances situational awareness and independent living capacity without technical onboarding friction.

items.title: Development of an AI-Based Awkward Working Posture Detection System Using the REBA Method with Edge Computing and Deep Learning Approaches in Industrial Workshops
items.abstract: Awkward working postures pose ergonomic risks in industrial workshops, particularly when combined with force, repetition, or prolonged exposure. This study implements a human-in-the-loop ergonomic assessment system integrating MediaPipe Pose, Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA), and edge computing. A Jetson Orin Nano processes uploaded media and Real Time Streaming Protocol (RTSP) camera streams. MediaPipe estimates 33 body landmarks to calculate six segment angles, while HSE personnel verify landmark placement and task factors before final scoring. The system stores assessment records in MySQL and displays them through a web dashboard. Four workshop postures involving low-workpiece handling, pipe maintenance, grinding, and welding demonstrate system functionality. System-derived REBA scores were 5 for squatting (Case A) and conditionally 5 for bending (Case B). Case B's final score was withheld because wrist visibility fell below 0.50. Observer scores were 7 and 5, respectively, with both cases classified as medium risk. Grinding and welding cases were evaluated without observer comparisons. Segment agreement reached 3/5 for Case A and 5/5 for Case B. During a two-hour RTSP test involving 93,729 frames, mean latency was 74.14 ± 19.64 ms, throughput reached 13.04 ± 2.08 FPS, and CPU/GPU utilization averaged 21.35%/57.71%. Findings demonstrate operational feasibility while identifying hip-landmark placement and occlusion as key sensitivity factors. However, these descriptive results neither establish measurement accuracy nor demonstrate reduced musculoskeletal disorder incidence. Further instrument-based validation across diverse postures and operating conditions remains necessary to establish measurement reliability and broader practical applicability.

items.title: Digital Health implementation experiences among nurses with and without Donor-Funded project affiliation in Kenya: An exploratory cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background Nurses’ participation and continuing support are important dimensions of electronic medical record (EMR) implementation. Evidence comparing these experiences across donor-funded and facility-employed nurses in Kenya is limited. This study compared reported design participation, pilot participation and ongoing training between these groups. Methods This exploratory secondary analysis used a cross-sectional, self-administered nursing survey conducted between March and May 2025. Analyses included 329 nurses: 190 reporting donor-funded project work and 139 identifying as facility employed without donor-funded project work. Design participation was the primary outcome; pilot participation and ongoing training and sensitisation were secondary outcomes. Agreement combined agree and strongly agree responses. Modified Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) with facility-clustered robust standard errors, adjusting for gender, age, education and facility tenure. Sensitivity analyses examined alternative sample definitions and modelling approaches. Results Agreement with design participation was 26.3% among donor-funded respondents and 47.5% among facility-employed respondents; corresponding proportions were 43.7% and 69.8% for pilot participation, and 96.8% and 55.4% for ongoing training. After adjustment, differences in design participation (PR 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.53–1.34) and pilot participation (PR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65–1.16) attenuated. Higher agreement with ongoing training persisted (PR 1.83, 95% CI 1.49–2.26), with consistent findings across sensitivity analyses. All respondents agreed with deployment training. Non-agreement with ongoing training among facility-employed respondents was predominantly neutral. Conclusions Work affiliation was associated with reported ongoing EMR training, while adjusted differences in design and pilot participation remained uncertain. Nursing managers should assess continuing support separately from deployment training and review training opportunities across work affiliations. These exploratory associations do not establish causal effects of employment or donor funding.

items.title: Digital Tools for the Detection of Dermatitis: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Contact dermatitis (CD) plays a significant role in occupational health due to its frequent occurrence and environmental triggers and is among the most common occupational diseases in Western countries. Despite its prevalence, occupational contact dermatitis (OCD) is often overlooked by occupational physicians, largely due to limited knowledge and a lack of validated detection tools. Advances in digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) offer promising opportunities for improving early detection, yet an overview of available digital tools and their effectiveness in dermatitis detection is lacking. A systematic review was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cinahl, and Scopus. The search focused on original studies published in peer-reviewed journals between 2014 and 2024. Forty-three studies evaluating digital tools for dermatitis detection were included, categorized as models (n = 31) or devices (n = 12). Models represent AI algorithms not yet in practical use, while devices are tools already implemented. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) were the most commonly used computational technique. Median sensitivity and specificity were 0.84 and 0.97 for all tools, 0.85 and 0.97 for models, and 0.78 and 0.97 for devices. The results provided in this review will serve as valuable input for the development of new tools to enhance early OCD detection.

items.title: Digital twins for intelligent intersections: A literature review
items.abstract: Digital twins (DTs) are increasingly proposed as a pathway toward safer, more adaptive, and more efficient intersection management, yet the literature remains conceptually uneven and methodologically fragmented. This review critically synthesizes 99 studies on DTs and closely related DT-enabling systems for intelligent intersections through five analytical dimensions, namely (i) Architectures and Integration Frameworks, (ii) Data Pipelines and Simulation Fidelity, (iii) Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) for Twin-Enabled Traffic Control, (iv) Human-Centered Safety, Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs), and Ethics, and (v) Scaling, Orchestration, and Network Integration. The review adopts a human-curated, multi-source screening and synthesis process in which large language models (LLMs) are used as bounded support tools for note taking, early screening, and draft synthesis, while all final interpretations, categorizations, and claims are validated against the source texts. Beyond summarizing recent work, the paper explicitly distinguishes digital models, digital shadows, and twin-complete systems, showing that many self-labeled transportation “digital twins” exhibit characteristics more consistent with digital shadows or advanced simulators, with only a smaller subset demonstrating operationally coupled twin functionality. The synthesis highlights major advances in modular architectures, multimodal sensing, co-simulation, reinforcement learning, and edge-to-cloud deployment, while also identifying persistent gaps in bidirectional synchronization, validation under real-world uncertainty, VRU-centered design, interoperability, governance, and large-scale deployment. The paper concludes with a sharper research agenda for moving DTs for intelligent intersections from promising prototypes toward operational, trustworthy, and human-centered urban systems.

items.abstract: Background: Digitalization has greatly transformed HRM all over the world, especially in the field of recruitment. However, Nigerian Public Institutions still experience difficulties in the adoption and implementation of digital recruitment systems. Objective: This study explored the challenges and opportunities of digitalization in the recruitment process in the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, Nigeria. Method: A quantitative case study was used, and data were collected from 30 human resource managers, information technology officers, and recruitment staff using a structured questionnaire given via Google Forms. The questionnaire included technical challenges, human factors, organizational factors, perceived potentials, and digital recruitment effectiveness measured on a 5-point Likert scale. Results: Descriptive results revealed moderate technical, human, and organizational challenges, while perceived potentials of digital recruitment showed higher mean scores ranging from 4.10 to 4.32, particularly for efficiency, transparency, and access to talent. Technical challenges (r = ?0.42) and human factors (r = ?0.35) were negatively correlated with digital recruitment effectiveness, whereas perceived potentials showed the strongest positive relationship (r = 0.85). Regression analysis revealed that perceived potentials had a significant positive effect (? = 0.78, p < 0.001), while technical challenges had a significant negative effect (? = ?0.35, p = 0.007). Conclusion: The findings highlight the need to improve technical infrastructure and strengthen the potential benefits of digital recruitment to facilitate more effective recruitment practices in Nigerian public institutions.

items.abstract: Context: As digital technologies advance rapidly, organizations require analytical frameworks that move beyond subjective intuition and interpret ease of use as a sociotechnical property that regulates business efficiency.Objective: The chapter analyzes the functional dimension of interactive design through the formalization of usability within the corporate environment of organizations.Method: An analytical-conceptual, descriptive and foundational approach was used, based on a systematic review of standards in computer ergonomics and in human-computer interaction (HCI) and on the operationalization of the construct into performance variables and indicators.The chapter examines the definition of usability provided by the ISO 9241-11 standard, its articulation with the ISO 9241-210 standard, Jakob Nielsen's five-attribute model, the conceptual distinction between usability and user experience (UX), and the operational principles of usable design in organizations.Results: According to the analysis, the systematic measurement of effectiveness, efficiency and satisfaction optimizes workflows and limits cognitive load, and these dimensions constitute the basis for the quantitative diagnosis of interaction.However, challenges remain, such as the terminological confusion between usability and UX and the difficulty of achieving operational consistency and reversibility.Conclusions: Usability is a necessary, though not sufficient, component of a competitive UX.The formal adoption of the ISO 9241-11 standard is suggested in order to reduce technical support costs, shorten users' learning curves and maximize the perceived value of the product.

items.title: Disinformation Online: Platform Imaginaries and Risks
items.abstract: For many years, digital platform companies like Facebook/Meta or Google have promoted a sociotechnical imaginary placing them at the forefront of a societal transformation toward a better world for all. The more recent association of platforms with risks that disinformation poses to individuals, groups, and democratic societies is one instance that calls such visions of the future into question. Against this backdrop, the chapter pursues two goals. First, it uses the problem of disinformation as a focal point for discussing the relationship between imaginaries and the notion of risk. Second, it analyzes how platforms’ Systemic Risk Assessment Reports, published for the first time in 2024 due to requirements of the European Union’s Digital Services Act (DSA), present a specific perspective on platform-related disinformation risks. The results show that a focus on bad actors as the cause of disinformation risks makes it possible for platforms to adhere to their established imaginary despite the imposed risk perspective. An alternative strategy is to paint the picture of a complex risk landscape in which the exact role of platforms remains opaque. This strategy is facilitated by the DSA’s ambiguity in defining systemic risks and feasible methods for quantifying them.

items.title: Driving style classification and trip scoring based on Machine learning
items.abstract: Driving styles reflect the behaviours of drivers and their tendencies to drive carefully, perform riskier manoeuvres or break traffic rules. They also play a significant role in traffic safety, as how calm or aggressive a person drives can determine how likely they are to enter an unsafe scenario and potentially crash. There are a wide variety of potential applications for a system that can identify driving styles and score driving trips, such as increasing drivers’ awareness of their shortcomings and adaptive insurance policies. To tackle this topic, this paper details a trip-scoring system using a Siamese network that inputs data grouped using k-means clustering. items.title: Educational Digital Games in K-12: Teacher Adoption, Barriers, and Benefits
items.abstract: Game-based learning (GBL) has interdisciplinary overlaps with media studies, and findings from educational research suggest that it can foster student engagement, critical thinking and 21st-century skills (Mao et al., 2022; Qian and Clark, 2016; Romero, Usart and Ott, 2015). However, its systematic adoption in formal K-12 education remains relatively low, particularly in the Slovak education system. This paper examines pedagogical acceptance of, and barriers to, the adoption of digital games among teachers in the regional education system of the Slovak Republic. The conceptual framework combines three complementary theoretical perspectives: Self-Determination Theory (SDT), which explains students’ intrinsic motivation through the fulfilment of psychological needs; technology acceptance models (TAM/UTAUT), which address teachers’ perceived usefulness and facilitating conditions; and Ertmer’s model of first- and second-order barriers. Quantitative data were collected from a quota sample of 105 teachers via computer-assisted personal interviewing (CAPI) in collaboration with the research agency IPSOS, and were analysed descriptively, with 95% confidence intervals for the proportion of respondents selecting each option. Teachers most frequently reported increased student motivation (54.3%), creative thinking (41.0%) and digital skills development (40.0%) as benefits of digital games, which suggests that many of them consider digital games pedagogically beneficial. Among non-users (n = 60), the most frequently reported reasons for non-use were a preference for traditional assessment (41.7%), an unclear connection to learning objectives (31.7%), a traditionally oriented school system (28.3%) and insufficient technical equipment (26.7%). Affective and competence-related second-order barriers, such as fear of losing control of the class, low digital literacy or fear of losing authority, were reported by relatively few teachers. These findings suggest that non-use is associated less with teachers’ resistance to technology than with assessment practices, curricular alignment and infrastructure, areas in which teachers’ pedagogical beliefs and institutional conditions are closely intertwined. Given the cross-sectional, self-report design, the results should be regarded as indicative; they point to the potential value of policy measures that address assessment and curriculum frameworks alongside teachers’ professional development.

items.title: Enacting Constructive Conflicts with AI Agents to Enhance Reconsideration among Novice Interaction Designers
items.abstract: Generative AI agents are increasingly used in interaction design to facilitate ideation, often following their own internal reasoning. These interactions tend to expand the design space. Our work explores an antagonistic role for design agents, prompting designers to engage with stakeholder tension. We built an antagonistic AI agent and examined the agent’s influence in a between-subjects experiment with 45 design students across three conditions: Self Reflection (unsupported review of the design proposal), Stepwise Guidance (written prompts that walk designers through a constructive-conflict framework), and Interactive Engagement (an AI agent that enacts the constructive-conflict framework interactively by synthesizing stakeholder pushback). The latter two conditions share the framework but differ in whether it is self-enacted or agent-enacted. Results show that, compared with Self Reflection, both the Stepwise Guidance and Interactive Engagement groups reported significantly higher self-reconsideration and made more improvements to their design proposals. Compared with Stepwise Guidance, the antagonistic agent introduced more conflictual perspectives, and participants in the Engagement condition generated and discarded more ideas. These findings suggest that an interactive agent that surfaces stakeholder pushback can support concrete design revision while keeping designers engaged with divergent perspectives.
